ff.info.fossil_frights.1.title: QUICK START
ff.info.fossil_frights.1.content:
1. Press Start to begin your first shift.

2. Go to the bookshelf and read your task book.

3. Finish every task before the five-minute shift ends.

4. When all tasks are complete, return to the start room and press Next Day to continue.
ff.info.fossil_frights.2.title: HOW TO PLAY
ff.info.fossil_frights.2.content:
You are a night-shift security guard in a museum. Each shift gives you a set of tasks, and you have five minutes to complete them.

The task book gives you the most important clues, but it will not explain the whole museum. Explore, learn the rooms, and remember useful routes.

You are not expected to win on your first try. Set a personal best, keep learning, and try to survive all 10 days.
ff.info.fossil_frights.3.content.1: Easy tasks usually require going somewhere, pressing a button, or checking a specific part of the museum.
ff.info.fossil_frights.3.content.2: Medium tasks are trickier and always require an item. Use your Storage Key to retrieve items, often from the basement, then bring each item to the location named in the task book.
ff.info.fossil_frights.3.content.3: Hard tasks are puzzles. Read the hints carefully, explore, and expect each one to work differently.
ff.info.fossil_frights.4.title: HAZARD FIXES
ff.info.fossil_frights.4.content:
Lights Out: pull the breaker to restore the lights.

Floor is Lava: reset the lava boiler to clean up the spill.

Flood: turn the water shutoff valve.

Curse: reset the ghost force field to repel the curse.

Security Gates: reset the security controller in the security office.
ff.info.fossil_heists.1.title: HOW TO PLAY
ff.info.fossil_heists.1.content: Thieves try to steal $1000 worth of merchandise while guards continuously stop them during a 10-minute night shift.
ff.info.fossil_heists.2.title: GUARDS
ff.info.fossil_heists.2.content:
Use a series of items: a night stick for killing, an ice cannon for freezing, plus glow traps and cameras for finding the thieves.

Guards are shown a list of all available items on the sidebar. Entries flash red if stolen and are crossed out if captured.

Guards secure any un-keyed loot by visiting and holding right click for 2 seconds.

If less than $1000 of loot is stolen before 10 minutes is up, the guards win.
ff.info.fossil_heists.3.title: THIEVES
ff.info.fossil_heists.3.content:
The thieves start in the vent. Review the sidebar list and try to steal at least $1000 of loot by collecting it and bringing it to the capture point at the museum entry.

On death, thieves lose any items they are carrying.

If thieves punch a guard, they are given a key and coin plus a short amount of invisibility to escape.
ff.info.fossil_heists.4.title: LOOT
ff.info.fossil_heists.4.content:
All loot locations are specified in the loot book.

Common loot is just 1 click to get.

Uncommon loot requires a key stolen from the guards, then that key must be used on a lock to get loot from the basement or elsewhere.

Rare loot usually requires an item from the basement and a little extra work, such as visiting an anvil.

Heavy loot is also 1 click to grab, but it applies extra slowness.
ff.info.fossil_heists.5.title: HAZARDS
ff.info.fossil_heists.5.content:
The hazards are the same as the base game, but in heists they can be activated by the thieves, either manually or by eating a Hazard Cookie.

Hazards give buffs to thieves, such as disabling cameras, revealing traps, or granting potion effects.

ff.settings.mode.party.title: Party Mode
ff.settings.mode.party.body:
Party mode opens the museum doors, letting players join and leave the game freely.

Recommended for players who have beaten the game, or large groups on a call, as there's only one task book and it's easy to miss learning the content.
ff.settings.mode.frights.body: Fossil Frights is a comprehensive 10-day challenge where you play as a museum security guard working 5-minute night shifts to complete various tasks around the museum.
ff.settings.mode.heists.title: Fossil Heists
ff.settings.mode.heists.body:
Fossil Heists is a two-team game mode where Guards must find and stop Thieves from stealing loot before the 10-minute night shift ends.

Recommended for players who know the museum layout and the base-game mechanics.

ff.plaques.1_raptor.label: Raptor
ff.plaques.1_raptor.title: VELOCIRAPTOR
ff.plaques.1_raptor.body:
Velociraptors were small dromaeosaurid theropods native to Central Asia with feathers and a large sickle-shaped claw on each hind foot.

This reptile was carnivorous, fast, and agile - likely using its claws for gripping prey rather than slashing.

§oNote: This skeleton has been scaled up to match its fictitious size from the Jurassic Park movie franchise.
ff.plaques.1_bronto.label: Bronto
ff.plaques.1_bronto.title: BRONTOSAURUS
ff.plaques.1_bronto.body:
The Brontosaurus was a huge quadrupedal herbivore native to western North America.

It had a relatively small head with peg-like teeth, a long neck, and a whip-like tail.

From head to tail, these gigantic animals could reach up to 21-23 meters and weighed 15-20 metric tons.
ff.plaques.1_t-rex.label: T-Rex
ff.plaques.1_t-rex.title: TYRANNOSAURUS REX
ff.plaques.1_t-rex.body:
The T-Rex was a large apex theropod predator from western North America.

It was carnivorous - likely both hunter and scavenger - with a massive skull, a bone-crushing bite force, and serrated teeth.

It was bipedal, walking on its powerful hind limbs, and had reduced forelimbs.
ff.plaques.1_dimetrodon.label: Dimetrodon
ff.plaques.1_dimetrodon.title: DIMETRODON
ff.plaques.1_dimetrodon.body:
The dimetrodon was a large sail-backed synapsid (not a dinosaur).

It was the apex predator of its ecosystems, in what is now North America and Central Europe.

Its distinct elongated neural spines formed a dorsal sail, likely used for thermoregulation and display.
ff.plaques.1_trike.label: Trike
ff.plaques.1_trike.title: TRICERATOPS (A.K.A. "TRIKE")
ff.plaques.1_trike.body:
The triceratops was a large ceratopsian herbivore with three facial horns and a broad bony frill native to western North America.

It likely used its horns and frill for defense, display, and intraspecies combat.

It fed on low-growing vegetation, and its beak and closely appressed front teeth formed a “dental battery” for shearing.
ff.plaques.1_gold-shark.label: Gold Shark
ff.plaques.1_gold-shark.title: GOLD SHARK
ff.plaques.1_gold-shark.body:
A rare variant of the tiger shark, found near river beds.

Exhibits a metallic, golden coloration derived from ingesting yellow sweaters dropped by nearby players.

Primary diet includes nautiluses, with preference for §o“golden” individuals.
ff.plaques.1_deep-sea.label: Deep Sea
ff.plaques.1_deep-sea.title: DEEP SEA CREATURES
ff.plaques.1_deep-sea.body:
Nautilus:

Marine cephalopod with a coiled external shell divided into gas-filled chambers for buoyancy control.


Giant Tube Worms:

They thrive in extreme environments on the seafloor, particularly around hydrothermal vents in the Pacific Ocean.
ff.plaques.1_plesiosaur.label: Plesiosaur
ff.plaques.1_plesiosaur.title: PLESIOSAUR
ff.plaques.1_plesiosaur.body:
The Plesiosaur was a marine reptile with broad bodies, four large flippers, and often very long necks with small heads.

It was carnivorous, feeding on fish and cephalopods in oceans worldwide.

It used flippers in a rowing motion for propulsion.
ff.plaques.1_footprints.label: Footprints
ff.plaques.1_footprints.title: FOOTPRINTS
ff.plaques.1_footprints.body:
Trace fossils preserving impressions of ancient animals' feet in sediment.

They formed when these animals walked on soft ground that later lithified (turned into solid rock).

These footprints provide us with information about the animals, such as their gait, speed, group movement, and behavior.
ff.plaques.sss_1.title: FOSSIL FRIGHTS TIPS
ff.plaques.sss_1.body:
§o1. Lower the forklift on day 1, it stays down.


2. Pay the crab to polish your key.
ff.plaques.sss_2.title: FOSSIL FRIGHTS TIPS
ff.plaques.sss_2.body:
§o3. Some hazards can be used to your advantage.

4. Golden Nautilus and Water Balloon are the most commonly needed items.
ff.plaques.ruins_basketball.title: RUINS BASKETBALL
ff.plaques.ruins_basketball.body:
The inhabitants of these ancient ruins are believed to have loved basketball.

Fossilized statues were found in positions consistent with the sport.

It is said that, judging by their short height, for 45,000 years they roamed the overworld, but never scored a basket...
ff.plaques.ruins_wishing-well.title: RUINS WISHING WELL
ff.plaques.ruins_wishing-well.body:
An ancient and magical wishing well that the copper inhabitants would use to get back home.

Theorized to be a predecessor to the “ender pearl stasis chamber”.

The golems built wells all across the overworld so that, at sunset, they could throw in a coin and the well would send them home.
ff.plaques.ruins_ruins.label: Ruins
ff.plaques.ruins_ruins.title: RUINS
ff.plaques.ruins_ruins.body:
Ancient unrestored ruins, transported directly from the primordial grounds and the birthplace of the copper golem.

Radiological dating and geological context suggests that these ruins are approximately 100,000 years old.
ff.plaques.ruins_artifacts.label: Artifacts
ff.plaques.ruins_artifacts.title: ARTIFACTS
ff.plaques.ruins_artifacts.body:
You are standing in an ancient tower which was restored from trail ruins.

Likely a place of worship for the inhabitants, the tower displayed these mysterious patterns that are said to hold their §odeepest and darkest secrets...
ff.plaques.ruins_ancient-cities.title: ANCIENT CITIES
ff.plaques.ruins_ancient-cities.body:
Copper golems exclusively built their ruins on top of ancient cities, above deep dark biomes.

Rumour has it that the sculk veins provided rich nutrients to the soil, aiding in their agriculture.

Other archaeologists believed it was for protection of their deepest treasures.
ff.plaques.ruins_fishing.label: Fishing
ff.plaques.ruins_fishing.title: FISHING
ff.plaques.ruins_fishing.body:
The copper golems' primary food source was spinach & ricotta stuffed salmon fillet, served over warm rice with a side of garlic bread.


Of course this is only an assumption... based on the fact that we found water near their homes.
ff.plaques.ruins_crops.title: CROPS
ff.plaques.ruins_crops.body:
While some societies of golems had their elaborate meals, the golems native to these temples subsisted on a simpler diet.

They are known to have grown potatoes and various fruits from the jungle.

Some evidence of riverine fish consumption is also noted, though this may have been from their taming of ocelots.
ff.plaques.ruins_jungle-temple.title: JUNGLE TEMPLE
ff.plaques.ruins_jungle-temple.body:
These reclusive jungle temples were created as tombs by a solitary culture of copper golems.

Due to the humidity of their environment, they seemed to have oxidized faster than other tribes.

Researchers theorize that death was held as a more important role in their society as a result.
ff.plaques.ruins_pots.title: DECORATED POTS
ff.plaques.ruins_pots.body:
These ancient pots display symbols carved into them by the copper golems.

It is believed they were stored underground as the moistness of the sculk kept the pots from cracking, while the warden guarded the pots and their secrets...
ff.plaques.ruins_ancient-portal.title: ANCIENT PORTAL
ff.plaques.ruins_ancient-portal.body:
This mysterious structure, found in ancient cities all over the overworld, has long puzzled explorers.

Forgotten by time, its original purpose and the people who created it remain unknown.


It is theorized by some to be a portal to the elusive Sift dimension...
ff.plaques.2_the-human.title: THE HUMAN
ff.plaques.2_the-human.body:
The Human

(Homo Sapiens)


Written by
Dr. SirSpacewalker



We build. We dig. We craft.

No claws, no wings, no natural armor; yet we reshape entire worlds with nothing but our hands and a few sticks.


The human is a strange creature.

Soft-bodied and slow, it should not survive.

And yet, it is the most dominant species on the planet.

Other beings wander. The jellyfish drifts without purpose; the amsel collects in silence. The dog shuffles forward, forgetting what it once was.

But the human builds toward something, always something just beyond the horizon.



They say life is simple. But watch one long enough and you'll see it's not. Watch them create new life.

Watch them go where no other human has gone yet. Watch them fight over and over again for what they think is right.



There is no potion that gives them wings, so they build towers instead.

Every limitation is just a problem waiting for a crafting table; the sky is definitely not one of them.


In the end, they reach the impossible - they always reach the impossible.

Not because they were the strongest species in the world, but because they refused to stop building until they were...

The history of the human will continue.
ff.plaques.2_ankylo.label: Ankylo
ff.plaques.2_ankylo.title: ANKYLOSAURUS
ff.plaques.2_ankylo.body:
The ankylosaurus was a heavily armored herbivore native to western North America.

 It had osteoderm plates covering its body, and a large bony tail club.

Its tail was likely used for high-force defensive strikes against predators.

It had a low browsing diet, with a beak and leaf-shaped teeth.
ff.plaques.2_sniffer.label: Sniffer
ff.plaques.2_sniffer.title: SNIFFER
ff.plaques.2_sniffer.body:
The Sniffer is an ancient, gentle creature from the prehistoric overworld.

It was once thought to be totally extinct, but was rediscovered by archaeologists inside of flooded ruins.

Sniffers have an extraordinary sense of smell and enjoy finding ancient seeds buried beneath the ground.
ff.plaques.2_burrowers.label: Burrowers
ff.plaques.2_burrowers.title: BURROWERS
ff.plaques.2_burrowers.body:
Many species of insects adapted to carve out niches inside of the bark of trees.

These niches would later be shared to some capacity with the first mammals, resembling the habitat of modern-day squirrels.
ff.plaques.2_fossils.title: FOSSILS
ff.plaques.2_fossils.body:
Fossils are the preserved remains and traces of animals & plants that lived very long ago.

They can form from bones, shells, footprints, and even leaves.

Fossils help scientists learn about ancient life and understand how Earth has changed over millions of years.
ff.plaques.3_hadean.title: HADEAN
ff.plaques.3_hadean.body:
The Hadean was defined by intense bombardment of the ancient, forming Earth.

One of these ancient collisions was with a protoplanet named Theia, which collided with Earth to form the Moon.

The surface was largely molten, and

slowly cooled into the Archean. Heavier elements like iron and nickel sank to the core, while lighter silicas rose to form the crust.

Very small zircon crystals from this eon have been preserved, but no known rocks survived from this time of history.
ff.plaques.3_archean.title: ARCHEAN
ff.plaques.3_archean.body:
The Archean was dominated by empty, vast oceans spanning most of the globe. High volcanism and plate tectonics gradually created the first ancient landmasses.

Life started in this Eon, with unicellular organisms deep in the seas.

The Archean atmosphere was vastly different to that of the present; methane rich, it would be more similar to Titan's atmosphere, a light hazy orange.

Asteroid impacts gradually slowed over the early Archean, to lower levels.
ff.plaques.3_proterozoic.title: PROTEROZOIC
ff.plaques.3_proterozoic.body:
The Proterozoic saw the rise of cyanobacteria, which lowered CO2 levels and released O2 - sparking the Great Oxygenation. 

The skies slowly turned blue, and this change in chemistry of the air also affected the water. Iron precipitated out

of the water to settle on the seafloors, later becoming banded iron formations that form the majority of mineable iron today.

The Proterozoic saw 2 ice ages, the Huronian and Cryogenian. The Huronian occurred because of the Great Oxygenation removing CO2 from the air,

lasting over 300 million years.

The Cryogenian, also known as Snowball Earth, saw the Earth (nearly) covered by ice towards the end of the Proterozoic. 

The Ediacaran Period at the end of this Eon saw the first large multicellular 

organisms, a trend that would spark the Cambrian Explosion of aquatic life.
ff.plaques.3_cambrian.title: CAMBRIAN
ff.plaques.3_cambrian.body:
The Cambrian commences the Phanerozoic Eon - also known as the Eon of Life. 

The Cambrian Explosion starts by most metrics the fossil record, when a sudden increase in ancient marine fossils permeated the rock record.

One of the most known specimens from this time was the trilobite. 

Named for having 3 distinct sections, the trilobite is a common arthopod class that persisted for hundreds of millions of years until the Permian-Triassic Extinction.
ff.plaques.3_ordovician.title: ORDOVICIAN
ff.plaques.3_ordovician.body:
The Ordovician saw a continuation of the evolution of large, multicellular life from the Cambrian.

One of the most famous genuses of this period, Endoceras, was a group of nautiloids that grew to enormous sizes, their shells over 3 metres long.

The Ordovician was also characterized by unusual bombardment within 30° of latitude to the equator; possibly signifying that Earth had a ring system for the duration of the bombardment period.

This may have sparked a mass extinction & ice age.
ff.plaques.3_silurian.title: SILURIAN
ff.plaques.3_silurian.body:
The Silurian saw warming from the Hirnantian Glaciation. 

Jawed fish and sharks began to evolve, and some sea creatures started to be more recognizable to us today.

The Late Silurian saw the Terrestrial Revolution, where plants - and later animals - found niches on land and developed terrestrial ecosystems. While some species had migrated to land in the Ordovician, the Late Silurian is when most did so.

Fungi were some of the first to make that transition.
ff.plaques.3_devonian.title: DEVONIAN
ff.plaques.3_devonian.body:
The Early Devonian saw the rise of prototaxites and other fungi* rise as the dominant terrestrial life.

As plants began to adapt, they encroached on the niches of the fungi, slowly greening the Earth's land surface to one more recognizable today.

The Late Devonian saw a series of extinctions, which together comprise one of the 5 "Big" Extinctions of Earth. It mainly affected the oceans, and the cause is unknown.

*§oPrototaxites are debated in their placement within the tree of life. Some consider it a unique extinct kingdom.
ff.plaques.3_carboniferous.title: CARBONIFEROUS
ff.plaques.3_carboniferous.body:
The Carboniferous, meaning "Coal-Bearing" in Latin, is defined by the rich coal seams that permeate the rocks today from this period. 

Oxygen-depleted swamps with high plant growth led to biomass accumulating in these swamps, which would

form peat. This peat was then lithified into coal over subsequent periods.

The whole of the Carboniferous took place during an ice age, where the tropics and temperate areas are what we often picture from this period.

Pangea started forming during this period.

Oxygen levels rose to 35%, meaning animal life could grow to gargantuan sizes, particularly insects.

Fires were much more dangerous because of the extra oxygen.
ff.plaques.3_permian.title: PERMIAN
ff.plaques.3_permian.body:
The Early Permian was a continuation of the Carboniferous, with the gradual decline of the long ice age that defined the last 2 periods. Conifers, which evolved in the Late Carboniferous, proliferated and spread widely in the Permian.

The Permian was marked by several extinctions, of which the two largest took place near the end of the period.

The Capitanian Extinction (~260 Mya) was likely caused by the Emeishan Traps, a large volcanic region in Sichuan, China.

Not long after, the Permian-Triassic Extinction, also known as the Great Dying, took place at 251.9 Mya.

A similar cause, this time it was the Siberian Traps that let loose vast fields of lava, polluting the atmosphere and acidifying the oceans.

It's theorized the ozone layer was severely damaged, due to recorded biological damage in fossils. It was the worst extinction in history, and took millions of years to recover from.

The Trilobite finally went extinct at this time.
ff.plaques.3_triassic.title: TRIASSIC
ff.plaques.3_triassic.body:
The Triassic was the hottest period of Earth in the Phanerozoic.

After the End-Permian Extinction, global temperatures were elevated due to the excess greenhouse gasses and Pangea's land configuration blocking moisture from the land's interior.

While present in some of the Permian, megamonsoons formed in the Panthalassic Ocean around Pangea and impacted the tropical areas with monumental intensity.

Triassic climate was extreme. The Carnian Pluvial Episode was a 2 million year event where rainfall and humidity affected almost the entire world; this sudden climactic shift is possibly related to the rise of the dinosaurs.

The climate dried again after the Carnian. The rifting of Pangea would lead to new volcanism in the heart of the super-continent, slowly forming the Atlantic.

The volcanism would trigger the Triassic-Jurassic Extinction, with similar but less-extreme impacts to the Permian-Triassic Extinction at the start of the period.
ff.plaques.3_jurassic.title: JURASSIC
ff.plaques.3_jurassic.body:
The Jurassic quickly rebounded from the mass extinction at its start, and as Pangea slowly started to break apart the temperatures of the planet cooled - though still far warmer than today.

The Jurassic only had one large extinction after this, when the Toarcian Oceanic Anoxic Event occurred 183 Mya, as oxygen levels in the oceans plummeted.

While there were dinosaurs in the Triassic, they grew more plentiful and diverse in the Jurassic.

The Pangean megamonsoon began to wane during the Jurassic as the supercontinent broke into Laurasia and Gondwana.

The breakup of the continents would lead to greater biodiversity going into the Cretaceous, and modern day.
ff.plaques.3_cretaceous.title: CRETACEOUS
ff.plaques.3_cretaceous.body:
The Cretaceous was a time of massive change. Pangea finally broke apart completely, the Atlantic Ocean was opening while the Tethys was closing, and continents slowly began to take their modern forms.

Many continents were partially submerged, case in point being North America. The central region, what would become the Prairies / Great Plains, flooded to form a biodiverse inland sea which resulted in many of the inland fossils seen in places like Alberta, Canada.

Flowering plants diversified and took over many of the gymnosperms' niches (ferns, conifers, etc).

The most famous dinosaurs existed in the Cretaceous, including the Velociraptor and T-Rex.

Forests were present at the poles, and snow was restricted to mountain peaks.

The Cretaceous may be most famous for what ended it. The K-Pg extinction, the 5th and most recent mass extinction, resultant from the Chicxulub Asteroid and possibly assisted by the volcanic Deccan Traps in India.
ff.plaques.3_paleogene.title: PALEOGENE
ff.plaques.3_paleogene.body:
The Paleogene was a time of climate transition. The K-Pg mass extinction 66 Mya had brief but devastating effects, cooling global temperatures and shrouding the skies.

Not long after, however, came the Paleocene-Eocene Thermal Maximum, or PETM. The PETM warmed the world drastically, with an unknown cause. Precipitation increased, but some dry areas remained.

The PETM is considered a way to study recent and replicatable climate change in the past, and is seen as a worst case scenario for Anthropogenic climate change.

Millions of years after, the planet began to cool as Antarctica separated and moved to the south pole, allowing ocean currents to isolate it and build up cold temperatures.

This sparked the Late Cenozoic Ice Age, ongoing today.

Many modern plants and animals can trace their ancestors to diversifying in the Paleogene.

The Paleogene and Neogene were once considered the Tertiary Period.
ff.plaques.3_neogene.title: NEOGENE
ff.plaques.3_neogene.body:
The Neogene is the penultimate period of the Phanerozoic eon, and during it the continents began to take their current shape today.

India was in the midst of colliding with Asia, Panama connected the Americas, Japan rifted from Asia, etc.

The Paleogene was marked by glacial and interglacial periods. One of those interglacials, the Pliocene Thermal Maximum (≈3.0 Mya) is viewed as a possibly middling-scenario for Anthropogenic climate change, in contrast to the more severe warming of the Eocene.

The Messinian Salinity Crisis 5.5 Mya saw most of the Mediterranean dry up, as tectonics forced Spain and Morocco together.

Temperatures as high as 80°C may have occurred in the basin, until erosion released the Atlantic back into the former sea in what was known as the Zanclean flood, carving the Strait of Gibraltar in only a matter of years.
ff.plaques.3_quaternary.title: QUATERNARY
ff.plaques.3_quaternary.body:
The Quaternary is the current geologic period, divided into the Pleistocene and Holocene.

The Pleistocene is what most people picture hearing the phrase "Ice Age," or at least the last glacial maximum of it.

Ice sheets covered much of North America and Europe, which periodically advanced and reteated in accordance with changes in how Earth orbits the Sun, called Milankovitch Cycles.

These ice sheets formed basins which filled with water, forming the Great Lakes and other water bodies like the Baltic Sea. Sea levels rose and fall depending on how much water was stored as ice sheets.

Early human species diversified in Africa, and learned how to use fire. They later spread across the world during the Last Glacial Maximum.

While different societies developed agriculture at different times, the Neolithic Revolution is considered to have happened around 10 years ago.

In those 10K years, humans (now only Homo Sapiens) began to dominate the planet. While some argue that our impact has been enough to classify recent history as a new geologic period (the Anthropocene) this proposal was rejected.

Nevertheless we have impacted Earth on the scale of the mass extinctions, and as I hope you can appreciate from my timeline, in the blink of an eye geologically.

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

This timeline has been a passion project for me and my academic studies, so I hope you enjoyed it!

-Endyblaze201
March 1st, 2026
ff.task_book.task.bathroom_leak.descript: There was a report of a flooded toilet in the 2nd floor bathroom. Not sure which stall; please find it and fix it. Usually flushing is a good temporary fix.
ff.task_book.task.check_ankylo.descripti: Check in on the Ankylosaurus skeleton, there are rumors some misfit added a tongue. Just casually walk by and make sure everything looks fine.
ff.task_book.task.check_security.descrip: Sometimes I forget we have a security system. We should really use it more. Please go down to the security office, and click on the security monitor to view the camera feed.
ff.task_book.task.climb_the_tower.descri: The tower gives a great view of the ruins, climb up to make sure everything around looks in order.
ff.task_book.task.count_shells.descripti: We try to keep a close eye, but we notice sometimes people are stealing the shells. Go check and make sure all 5 of them are on the display table.
ff.task_book.task.count_toes.description: People keep standing on the giant T-Rex footprint and messing it up. Please go make sure you can still count all 3 toes.
ff.task_book.task.dig_sand.description.0: There's a sandbox for kids to dig in the desert temple, but there's too much sand piled in the center. Can you move it around? We have no shovels, so just use your hand.
ff.task_book.task.dive_into_well.descrip:
Dive into the wishing well and count the Dino Coins for me... but don't you dare collect them! They're mine! All mine. 

If there's more than 20, bring them to my desk. Otherwise,
ff.task_book.task.fire_pottery.descripti: The pottery firing display in the trail ruins keeps going out. Test the ignition switch to ensure it's functional still. Don't stand in the fire, we're not insured.
ff.task_book.task.fix_cracked_egg.descri: The sniffer egg appears to be slightly cracked. Find it and fix it; likely all you have to do is poke it a bit until the cracks are no longer visible.
ff.task_book.task.fix_mars.description.0: The model of Mars in the observatory is crumbling, can you please go try and put it back together?
ff.task_book.task.lock_register.descript: Please lock the cash register in the gift shop, usually just hitting it does the trick.
ff.task_book.task.make_some_noise.descri: The warden is very lonely and never sees anyone... but luckily he has great hearing. Go dance around him so he can hear you, that should be enough to cheer him up!
ff.task_book.task.polish_bell.descriptio: The service bell in the gift shop looked smudged, please polish it and make sure it still rings.
ff.task_book.task.reset_fountain.descrip: Please reset the fountain in the aviary, the user manual recommends doing it every so often to keep the pipes clean.
ff.task_book.task.reset_salt_level.descr: Check the saline levels for the tank, if 'WARN' or 'ALERT' press the reset button and levels should return to 'OK'.
ff.task_book.task.static_buildup.descrip: The lightning simulator in Triassic exhibit appears to be malfunctioning and creating a build up of static electricity. Please press the reset button so it may discharge.
ff.task_book.task.swat_flies.description: The fresh cow manure in the feces exhibit keeps attracting flies, please swat them away. Just swing your hands wildly... I'm sure it'll scare them off.
ff.task_book.task.sweep_popcorn.descript: Someone spilt their popcorn in the theatre, please sweep it up. Unfortunately our broom is missing, so just use your hands or something?
ff.task_book.task.tnt_test.description.0: Rumors are the Precision Excavation Demonstration Unit5000 is broken again. Instead of just demonstrating with fake TNT, it's actually blowing things up. Please test the detonator and make
ff.task_book.task.tnt_test.description.1:
sure the TNT lights. 

Just be sure you don't die! It would be a lot of paperwork.
ff.task_book.task.toilet_clog.descriptio: Not sure where but apparently a muffin was shoved in a toilet? I'd start by checking the one near the cafe. Please flush the muffin and hopefully the leak goes away.
ff.task_book.task.visit_archean.descript: I like to keep the dripstone spiky but the kids keep touching them. Walk through the Archean exhibit near the start of Earth's Timeline, and make sure everything is looking pointy!
ff.task_book.task.visit_jurassic.descrip: Please walk through the Jurassic period near the middle of the Earth's Timeline exhibit, there are rumors people have been picking leaves off the cycads.
ff.task_book.task.visit_neogene.descript: There was a report of a spill in the Neogene exhibit near the end of the timeline, it should have been cleaned up by now... but give it a walkthrough and take a peak?
ff.task_book.task.visit_silurian.descrip:
The start of the Silurian was a cold and dry place. Like my heart, ha! You know what, go check it out, let the excitement for the job be ripped out of you. 

It's around the middle
ff.task_book.task.water_temp.description: The carnivorous plants are very sensitive to water that is too cold or hot. Test the temperature of the water in the terrarium? A simple dip of the toes should be good enough.
ff.task_book.task.plesiosaur_clone.descr:
Wow. So you really made it 10 days. Most people quit after 2. Well, technically I fire them. Anyway.....

(Multiple Pages)
I think I can trust you with this. I left the secret laboratory doors open. It's between the rings of Earth up on the top floor, in the Ordovician.
I'm going to need you to clone a dino for me. I'm out of microfiber cloths; you'll have to flatten a sponge with the anvil, then use that to scrub the plesiosaur egg for DNA.
Now put that DNA cloth in the DNA analyzer, it's that machine with the big empty tank. If it works it will start running, and you'll see a dino in the cloning vat.
Next the check the screen of the Clonomat, it will specify an item it needs. Go grab and toss it into the centrifuge; if the items are correct it will start spinning.

And uhm, yeah. That's it... If you get this done I'll hire you full-time. I'll start paying you, even. 

Oh! I almost forgot, the Clonomat produces a plushie as a byproduct. Feel free to keep it, I've got hundreds already.

Wow, is it getting hot in here, please reset the A/C. The controller is near the ceiling in the aviary. I lost the manual, but I think there are four buttons to restart the fan.
ff.task_book.task.basketball_dance.descr: Coppy loves to listen to music, it helps keep him from oxidizing. We have some records in the basement. Grab a disc, play a tune and dance with him! If your moves are
groovy enough he'll toss you a basketball. Go dunk a basketball in the ruins basketball court to honor his gift.
ff.task_book.task.defrost_freezer.descri: Ugh, my burgers keep getting freezer burnt. Can you please defrost the staff room fridge? Just open the door and the defrost lever should be on the back wall. If your feet get cold,
you can use the anvil to form some leather into a pair of boots.
The evolution statues from the human exhibit appear to have unfrozen and escaped! Please track them down in the correct order and send them back to the exhibit! They could not have
gotten far, so start with the 2nd floor and see if you can find them. Again please send them back in the correct evolutionary order the exhibit usually has them displayed in.
ff.task_book.task.feed_the_bats.descript: So we ran out of bugs... but if we don't feed the bats they'll die… So maybe grab some dried up ladybugs from the tree habitat exhibit and use that as bat food?
ff.task_book.task.fertilize_plant.descri: One of the plants is wilting on the 2nd floor, and its leaves are grey. Water is not bringing it back to life, do you mind giving it some fertilizer?
ff.task_book.task.glowberry_trees.descri:
Please water both glowberry trees. 

DO NOT EAT THE GLOWBERRIES! I REPEAT DO NOT EAT THE GLOWBERRIES!
ff.task_book.task.holy_grail.description: Legend has it the ancient city is home to the long-lost Holy Grail, a pot of great importance.
I need you to bring it a sacrificial golden nautilus, hopefully it unlocks some magical powers!
The grail in question will be unique. The carvings on it should be recorded elsewhere... our archaeologists noted sherds of particular interest in the tower. Maybe the two are related?
ff.task_book.task.hoveraptor.description: Did you know hoverboards were invented back in the Jurassic period to allow dinosaurs like the velociraptor to travel around quickly? Technically, it was never proven,

but a person's misguided belief. You know what... there's some scrap metal in the basement. Bring it to the anvil and forge it into a hoverboard, then bring it to the velociraptor and let him ride it!
ff.task_book.task.pig_wrangler.descripti: Every time I think I've solved that pig problem, the little escape artist proves me wrong... He's gone again! He's probably somewhere near the ruins exhibit, though he has been known to wander farther afield.

Grab a carrot cake from the cafe and use it to lure him back to the pen behind the ruins tower. Once he's safe, feed him the cake. He's such a good boy. Well... except for all the escaping.

If you can't find him, climb the tower and look through the spyglass.
ff.task_book.task.return_the_key.descrip: I like to move the Super Secret Key between a few locations to keep it safe. Currently, it's in the treasure chest. Can you grab it and move it to my vault?
ff.task_book.task.skincare_routine.descr: The Brontosaurus loves his skincare; he wants to look his best before the museum opens up. Please splash his face with water to keep him moist!
ff.task_book.task.star_gazing.descriptio: Since you're the only one here at night, I'll need you to go check which star patterns are visible. Look through the telescope and check which constellation you can see. Compare it with the images on the
walls, and mark which one is visible. You should note depending on the time of year the constellations may appear rotated.
ff.task_book.task.the_lost_code.descript: The fabled code. A combination of cotton blue and candy pink lost forever in the depths of the jungle temple... too difficult to crack, and forever lost to history.
Anyway please crack the code this shift, or you're fired.
ff.task_book.task.ancient_portal.descrip: The portal in the deep dark is emitting a bad odor, can you please toss in some febreeze? Be careful however: if you shake the canister it may explode, and cause the portal
to light. It's dangerous entering the portal as it could teleport you somewhere you don't want to be... or maybe you do want to be there? I don't care, do what you want.
ff.task_book.task.bring_brush.descriptio: Someone keeps stealing the brush from the sandpit on the 2nd floor near the aviary, can you please grab a spare one from the restoration room in the basement?
ff.task_book.task.brush_delivery.descrip: Are you kidding me?! ANOTHER BRUSH IS STOLEN! GRR! Grab one from the basement restoration room and bring it into the pyramid in the trail ruins. Just toss it in the pit.
ff.task_book.task.chlorinify.description: With all these spills people keep getting sick from the aquarium water. Can you toss a chlorine tablet in the drain at the bottom of the tank output in the basement?
ff.task_book.task.coffee_top_up.descript: The basement coffee machine ran out, please fill it up before the morning shift starts. I don't want our employees falling asleep before they even start their day.
ff.task_book.task.cool_it.description.0:
There's some melted ice in the Quaternary exhibit at the end of the timeline, and it's supposed to be ice. 

We've got dry ice in storage, toss some in the puddle?
ff.task_book.task.credit_reel.descriptio: The film reel was recently damaged and thrown out. Can you please fetch a spare reel from the boss's office and bring it to the projector in the theatre?
ff.task_book.task.feed_parrot.descriptio: The parrot escaped, and we're out of bird feed. Birds are like fish... right? Grab some fish food and put it in the parrots empty nest, hopefully he returns.
ff.task_book.task.feed_the_fish.descript: Please feed the fish in the aquarium. Fish food is in the basement, all you have to do is add it to the automatic fish feeder.
ff.task_book.task.feed_the_plants.descri: One of the carnivorous plants has gotten very vicious, and keeps attacking customers. Please feed him some cotton candy to help him calm down.
ff.task_book.task.fix_sculker.descriptio: The ancient city sculk generator is on the fritz, likely some more scrap metal should fix it right up. Grab some and bring it down to the Sculker; it should reactivate.
ff.task_book.task.heat_it_up.description: Our "artificial" lava in the Hadean exhibit is supposed to smoke, but reports say one of them stopped. Grab a fire tablet from the basement and toss into the
correct lava pool, so it starts up again. Fire tablets are expensive, so make sure you choose the right lava - whichever is smoking the least.
ff.task_book.task.nautilus_guard.descrip: The Gold Shark is staring at the nautilus. Stand between the two and equip a gold nautilus on your head, that should divert his attention.
ff.task_book.task.picnic_with_trike.desc: The triceratops skeleton has requested you join him for a picnic. Only problem is he doesn't like to share his food. Bring a snack and eat it with him: you can
have a free cookie from the cafe if you'd like.
ff.task_book.task.popcorn_buckets.descri: We're out of popcorn buckets in the theatre concession booth. There should be some more of them in storage, mind bringing one up? Just toss it in the popcorn machine.
ff.task_book.task.refill_coffee.descript: Apparently the cafe is out of coffee. There should be some beans or instant coffee or something in the basement. See what you can find, and dump it in the machine.
ff.task_book.task.refill_ice.description: The drink vending machine in the cafe seems to have lost power and is defrosting. Can you grab some dry ice and refill the machine?
ff.task_book.task.replenish_soap.descrip: People keep stealing the soap from the second floor bathroom. If the glass soap case is empty, please grab a new bar of soap and toss it into the glass dish.
ff.task_book.task.restock_plushies.descr: The Skeleton plushies are out of stock in the gift shop, mind grabbing one from storage and bringing it up? Toss it in the open box on the floor.
ff.task_book.task.revitalize_coral.descr: Pink coral is very delicate, we have a supply of Pink Jelly in the basement. Can you please grab some and smear it onto the pink fan coral in the Tide Pool Touch Tank?
ff.task_book.task.shark_bait.description: The Gold Shark may look like a sculpture, but some evil force makes him come to life. The only way to stop the shark is to feed him a golden nautilus sometimes. Do it. Or else....
ff.task_book.task.smelly_toilet.descript: Unfortunately our janitor is out sick, and one of the toilets on the first floor is super smelly... Can you toss some febreeze in it?
ff.task_book.task.sponge_up_spill.descri: There was a spill on the aquatic table, we put out a bucket. Can you bring up a dry sponge to mop up the mess?
ff.task_book.task.wash_muddy_sherd.descr: I accidentally ordered a box of muddy sherds, it's sitting in one of the ruins. Can you grab one and toss it into the washbasin in the ancient city?
ff.task_book.task.water_crops.descriptio: Can you please water the crops in the trail ruins exhibit, next to the jungle temple? Grab a water balloon and toss it onto the crops.
